minutes.headline: Steering committee heard town land and building options for a gathering space and tested draft master plan goals; no votes beyond adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee heard a select board member describe town-owned land and the municipal building plans as options for a public gathering space. Consultants presented draft values and goals and asked for feedback on housing, economic development, transportation and finance. A member reviewed the 2002 master plan, and the group settled the May 30 public meeting at Smoke Stack. The only formal vote was adjournment.

public_comment.topic: A speaker said the committee charge lists six at-large members and the vacancy count looked wrong, and that members had not been sworn in.
Suggested a townwide training session for boards and committees on how to run a meeting.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn; roll call taken, all members answering aye.

budget_items.topic: Cost of 30 School Street park/gathering space
budget_items.what_was_said: The speaker said the prior plan was estimated at roughly this cost for about 2 acres, noting prevailing wage; funding for construction documents failed at town meeting.
Rehabilitating the building was estimated at a large sum, about half of it code upgrades.

budget_items.topic: New town office annex and Ritter work
budget_items.what_was_said: HVAC and wall remodel at Ritter would cost a couple million, and a new office building was estimated at a price per square foot.

budget_items.topic: Debt exclusion impact on tax bills
budget_items.what_was_said: Building projects would need a debt exclusion, which raises the tax bill for 20 years or more.
ARPA funds have been committed to design the municipal building plan for renderings and cost estimation.

budget_items.topic: Solar at old landfill revenue split
budget_items.what_was_said: The speaker personally proposed splitting future solar revenue between the operating fund and buildings.

budget_items.topic: Loss of aid tied to fewer students
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the district lost money because of fewer children in the apartment area.
A member said a balance of Chapter 90 funds is unspent and could support sidewalk work.

budget_items.topic: Water department pump upgrade and stormwater
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the water department is proposing a pump upgrade for filtration and that stormwater will need major spending.
A 2.5 override question for schools is on the ballot, and its outcome could affect future town-side overrides.
A member said school maintenance needs could easily absorb a large sum and the town lacks money for it.
figures_as_heard: a quarter of a million dollars

budget_items.topic: Tax levy from large vs small homes
budget_items.what_was_said: A member compared the levy from a high-value home at the current rate with ten smaller homes.

decisions.decision: Public meeting set for May 30 at 6:00 p.m. at Smoke Stack coffee roaster, posted like any town meeting.
Chair to circulate a Doodle poll to schedule an additional steering committee meeting to review survey wording.
Members to take a pre-launch survey individually and submit comments, then discuss in a posted public meeting, to avoid open meeting law problems.
Survey to focus on asking residents how to achieve the goals rather than whether they agree; consultants to revise the goals with feedback.
Chair and consultant to work on a flyer for May 4 town meeting advertising the May 30 event.
A member will speak directly to the library director about hosting the 4x8 aerial town map.

what_happened.line: The committee set a public meeting for May 30 at 6:00 p.m. at Smoke Stack coffee roaster, to be posted like any town meeting.
A select board member described town-owned land and the municipal building plans as options for a public gathering space, including debt exclusion and ARPA-funded design.
Consultants presented draft values and goals; the survey will ask residents how to achieve the goals, and the consultants will revise them with feedback.
Members will take the pre-launch survey individually and discuss it in a posted public meeting, to avoid open meeting law problems.
The only formal vote was adjournment; no other votes were taken.

why_it_matters: Any gathering space or municipal building would need a debt exclusion, which raises tax bills for 20 years or more and would come to residents as a ballot vote.
The survey and the May 30 public meeting are the stated ways residents can shape the draft master plan goals on housing, economic development, transportation and finance.

A Doodle poll for an added steering committee meeting to review the survey wording.
